Introduction
The
following
document
is
the
specification
of
the
REST
API
for
Fraud
Management.
It
includes the model definition as well as all available operations. In the telecommunications
industry, fraud detection and prevention are critical to protecting both service providers
and
their
customers.
As
digital
transactions
increase
and
new
attack
vectors
emerge,
Communication Service Providers (CSPs) need a standardized approach to evaluate fraud
risk across multiple dimensions including identity verification, network authentication, and
behavioral analysis.
The Fraud Management API provides a standardized mechanism for evaluating fraud risk
associated with a telecommunications customer or transaction. The API enables requesting
parties (such as merchants, banks, or internal systems) to submit fraud evaluation requests
and receive comprehensive risk assessments. The API consists of a task-based resource
that coordinates multiple fraud signal checks in a consistent manner. A fraud evaluation is
performed
based
on
criteria
specified
by
the
requester,
covering
risk
profiling,
network
authentication, fraud scoring, and profile matching.
A
canonical
JSON
example
of
EvaluateFraudRisk
(request
and
response
shape,
polymorphic attributes, and nested criteria) is provided in the API documentation package
as
resource-samples/EvaluateFraudRisk.json
. The examples in this user guide and
the
operation/notification
samples
follow
the
same
schema
patterns
and
TM
Forum
example
rules:
@baseType
appears
only
for
functional
inheritance
(in
this
API,
typically
ContactMedium
for phone, email, and geographic-address contact mediums, and
Event
for event payloads). It is not set to the same value as
@type
, nor used for technical base
classes such as
EntityRef
or
PartyRef
.
The Fraud Management API goal is to provide fraud risk evaluation capabilities, with 1 task
resource:
•
EvaluateFraudRisk
EvaluateFraudRisk allows to:
•
request a fraud risk evaluation for a target identifier (e.g. phone number) against a set
of configurable fraud evaluation criteria. The requester provides the target, criteria, and
related
party
information
and
expects
to
receive
a
comprehensive
fraud
evaluation
result.
•
in the request, the following attributes could/must be filled:
◦
fraudTargetIdentifier,
the
contact
medium
(e.g.
PhoneContactMedium
with
phoneNumber
) identifying the subject of the fraud evaluation

The API supports both synchronous and asynchronous execution modes:
•
POST may return
200
(results without persisting a task) or
201
(results with a persisted
task), depending on server policy.
•
The user guide example aligns with a persisted task for auditing (
201 Created
).
Fraud Management API could be used:
•
By merchants or banks to verify customer identity during transactions

Fraud Management API performs the following operations on EvaluateFraudRisk:

◦
EvaluateFraudRisk creation
◦
EvaluateFraudRisk state change
The following Assumptions were considered in the development of this document:
•
The Fraud Management system has access to telecom subscriber data (SIM, device, line
information)
•
The system has access to network authentication services for call verification
•
The system has access to fraud scoring engines and profile matching databases
Lifecycle
The state machine specifying the typical state change transitions is provided below. This is
standard task based resource lifecycle:
Fraud Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2025. All Rights Reserved.
Page 3
State
Definition
InProgress
The In Progress state is when the fraud evaluation task is
currently being processed. The system is actively performing
the requested fraud checks (risk profiling, network
authentication, scoring, profile matching).
Done
The fraud evaluation has been completed. All requested fraud
checks have been performed and results are available for the
requester.
TerminatedWithError
The fraud evaluation task could not be correctly completed.
The evaluation is not available or partial due to system errors
or unavailable fraud signal sources.

What Happens During Evaluation
1. Direct Checks on the Phone Number (fraudTargetIdentifier):
•
How long has this SIM been active?
•
Is this number using call forwarding?
•
Recent SIM swaps?
•
Service status verification
2. Pattern Matching (fraudProfileMatchCriteria):
The API evaluates each provided profile element against fraud databases and watchlists:
•
Email "
john.doe@gmail.com
" matches 85% with known fraudster email pattern
•
Address "123 Fake Street" appears in fraud address database
•
Name "John Doe" is identified as a generic name often used in fraud attempts
Understanding Match Elements
The
matchElement
property
in
the
response
identifies
which
specific
input
field
was
evaluated. Match elements correspond to the
fraudProfileMatchCriteria
inputs:
•
emailAddress
— matches the
email
(
EmailContactMedium
)
emailAddress
value
•
name
— matches the
partyName
string
•
address
— matches the
address
(
GeographicAddressContactMedium
) input
•
phoneNumber
— if included in
fraudProfileMatchCriteria

Fraud Evaluation Criteria
Optional vs Required Fraud Checks
Not all fraud evaluations need all checks. The separate criteria schemas allow:
•
Mix-and-match
- Include only the fraud detection methods you need
•
Conditional logic
- Different fraud scenarios can use different combinations
•
Future
expansion
-
New
fraud
detection
methods
can
be
added
without
modifying
existing schemas
Fraud Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2025. All Rights Reserved.
Page 8
Available fraud check types:
•
fraudRiskProfileCriteria
•
fraudNetworkAuthenticationCriteria
•
fraudScoreCriteria
•
fraudProfileMatchCriteria
Match Score Format
The match score is represented as a string to support multiple scoring formats used by
different fraud detection systems:
•
Percentage strings:
"90", "85.5"
•
Decimal confidence scores:
"0.90", "0.85"
•
Categorical ratings:
"HIGH", "MEDIUM", "LOW"
•
Qualified scores:
"90-EXACT", "75-FUZZY"
Example Use Cases:
•
High-sensitivity applications (banking)
•
Risk management systems
•
Hybrid systems combining numerical and qualitative indicators
SIM Swap & Replacement Checks (Post-Issuance)
Scenario:
A telecom operator receives a SIM replacement request for phone number "91-
98765-43210". Per TRAI’s mandated six-step authentication procedure, the operator must
verify the request is legitimate before processing. Additionally, the system must enforce
the seven-day porting restriction after a SIM swap or replacement.
Regulatory Context:
TRAI has mandated a six-step authentication procedure for processing SIM replacement:
1.
Photo Capture by the agent
2.
Face match with Aadhaar photo
3.
Biometric scan (fingerprint and iris)
4.
Aadhaar-based OTP to the registered number
5.
Matching old SIM details with KYC documents
Fraud Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2025. All Rights Reserved.
Page 9
6.
Tele-verification through a personalized question set
Additionally, a Unique Porting Code (UPC) cannot be allocated if the request is made within
seven days of a SIM swap or replacement, preventing fraudsters from quickly porting away
after a fraudulent SIM swap.

What Happens During Evaluation
1. SIM Swap & Tenure Checks (fraudRiskProfileCriteria):
•
Was a SIM swap recently performed on this number?
•
How
long
has
the
current
SIM
been
active?
(A
very
recent
SIM
with
an
immediate
replacement request is suspicious)
•
Is the line tenure consistent with a genuine long-term customer?
•
Is call forwarding enabled? (Fraudsters often enable forwarding to intercept OTPs)
•
Is the service currently active?
2. Network Authentication (fraudNetworkAuthenticationCriteria):
•
Call
verification
to
the
registered
number
confirms
the
legitimate
subscriber
is
reachable
•
Supports the Aadhaar-based OTP step in TRAI’s six-step process
3. Profile Matching (fraudProfileMatchCriteria):
•
Verify
that
the
name
and
address
provided
at
the
retail
outlet
match
existing
KYC
records
•
Supports step 5 of TRAI’s procedure — matching old SIM details with KYC documents

IMEI & Device Checks
Scenario:
A telecom operator needs to validate the IMEI of a device being activated on a
new connection. The IMEI must be checked against the CEIR (Central Equipment Identity
Register) via the Sanchar Saathi platform to ensure it is not stolen, cloned, or blacklisted.
Regulatory Context:
The
Sanchar
Saathi
platform
supports
IMEI
validation,
allowing
users
and
authorities
to
verify
the
IMEI
number
of
a
device.
Operators
also
check
IMEI
against
the
CEIR
(Central
Equipment Identity Register) to block stolen or blacklisted devices from being activated on
new connections.

What Happens During Evaluation
1. Device Validation (fraudRiskProfileCriteria):
•
Is the device IMEI recognized and valid?
•
How
long
has
this
device
been
in
use
on
the
network?
(A
brand-new
IMEI
appearing
with a used SIM may indicate a stolen device)
•
What is the SIM tenure associated with this connection?
•
Is the service currently active on this number?
2. CEIR / Sanchar Saathi Cross-Check (implicit in fraud scoring):
•
The fraud scoring engine checks the device IMEI against the CEIR blacklist
•
Stolen, lost, or cloned devices flagged in the central registry will result in a high fraud
score
•
Devices reported by users via the Sanchar Saathi portal are automatically reflected in
CEIR

tenure
of

means

(24

and
a

should
block

TAFCOP — Connection Limit Check
Scenario:
A telecom operator receives a new connection request from an individual. Before
provisioning,
the
operator
must
verify
through
the
TAFCOP
(Telecom
Analytics
for
Fraud
Management and Consumer Protection) portal whether the applicant’s identity documents
have
been
used
to
register
excessive
mobile
connections,
which
may
indicate
identity
fraud or SIM farming.
Regulatory Context:
The Sanchar Saathi platform includes features to let users check if their names have been
used to register additional mobile connections. Through the TAFCOP portal, operators and
users
can
verify
how
many
connections
are
registered
against
one
identity,
and
flag
or
disconnect excess connections.

What Happens During Evaluation
1. Identity Cross-Referencing (fraudProfileMatchCriteria):
•
Does the name, email, and address match existing records across operators?
•
How many active connections are currently registered against this identity?
•
Are there connections under slight name or address variations (fuzzy matching)?
2. Payment Method Check (fraudRiskProfileCriteria):
•
What payment method is associated with existing connections? (SIM farms often use
the same prepaid payment method across multiple connections)
3. TAFCOP Cross-Check (implicit in fraud scoring):

data
to
determine
the
total
number
of
connections registered to this identity
•
Connections exceeding regulatory limits are flagged
•
Previously disconnected or flagged connections under the same identity are factored
into the score

Support of polymorphism and extension
patterns
Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by
means
of
a
list
of
generic
meta-attributes
that
we
describe
below.
Polymorphism
in
collections
occurs
when
entities
inherit
from
base
entities,
for
instance
a
BillingAccount
and SettlementAccount inheriting properties from the abstract Account entity.
Generic
support
of
polymorphism
and
pattern
extensions
is
described
in
the
TMF
API
Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).
The
@type
attribute
provides
a
way
to
represent
the
actual
class
type
of
an
entity.
For
example, within a list of Account instances some may be instances of BillingAccount where
other
could
be
instances
of
SettlementAccount.
The
@type
gives
this
information.
All
resources
and
sub-resources
of
this
API
have
a
@type
attributes
that
can
be
provided
when this is useful.
The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance an AccountRef
object)
to
explicitly
denote
the
actual
entity
type
of
the
referred
class.
Notice
that
in
reference
entities
the
@type,
when
used,
denotes
the
class
type
of
the
reference
itself,
such as BillingAccountRef or SettlementAccountRef, and not the class type of the referred
object.
However
since
reference
classes
are
rarely
sub-classed,
@type
is
generally
not
useful in reference objects.
The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined
properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.
The
@baseType
attribute
gives
a
way
to
provide
explicitly
the
base
class
of
a
given
resource that has been extended through functional inheritance. Do not set @baseType to
the same value as @type, or to technical classes such as Entity, EntityRef, Extensible, or
Addressable. For this API’s published examples, @baseType is populated only where that
inheritance
applies
(for
example
ContactMedium
for
contact-medium
subtypes,
and
Event
for
event
subtypes).
Use
Characteristic
as
@baseType
only
when
a
concrete
characteristic
subtype
extends
Characteristic
(not
when
@type
is
simply
Characteristic
).

This

(examining SIM/device tenure, payment history), network-

and

fraud

optional based on the fraud evaluation requirements.

FraudEvaluationCriteria sub-resource fields
Specifies
the
evaluation
criteria
and
checks
that
should
be
performed
during
the
fraud
assessment process. This includes defining which fraud detection methods to apply, such
as
risk
profile
analysis
(examining
SIM/device
tenure,
payment
history),
network-level
authentication verification, fraud scoring algorithms, and customer profile matching against
known fraud patterns. Each criterion can be configured as required or optional based on
the fraud evaluation requirements.
fraudNetworkAuthenticationCr
iteria
A FraudNetworkAuthenticationCriteria. Indicates if
network authentication criteria is mandatory for fraud
evaluation.
fraudProfileMatchCriteria
A FraudProfileMatchCriteria. Defines the customer profile
information elements that should be used for matching
analysis against known fraud patterns and watchlists.
Specifies which customer identifiers and contact details
(such as email address, name, and physical address)
should be compared during the profile matching process
to identify potential matches with fraudulent profiles or
suspicious entities previously flagged in fraud databases.
fraudRiskProfileCriteria
A FraudRiskProfileCriteria. Defines whch customer and
account risk profile factors should be evaluated during
fraud detection analysis. Specifies whether to examine
factors such as SIM card tenure, device tenure, line tenure,
payment method type, call forwarding configuration,
service activation status, and recent SIM swap history.
Each factor can be selectively enabled or disabled to
customize the risk assessment scope based on the fraud
detection scenario.
fraudScoreCriteria
A FraudScoreCriteria. Defines the requirements and
configuration for fraud risk scoring during the evaluation
process. Specifies whether fraud scoring is mandatory for
the evaluation and whether detailed explanations should
be provided to describe the factors and reasoning behind
the calculated fraud score. This allows customization of
the fraud scoring depth and transparency based on
business requirements or regulatory compliance needs.

FraudEvaluationResult sub-resource fields
Contains the comprehensive results from all fraud evaluation checks that were performed
according to the specified criteria. This aggregates outcomes from multiple fraud detection
methods including risk profile analysis results (tenure information, payment types, service
status),
network
authentication
verification
status,
calculated
fraud
risk
scores
with
explanations, and profile matching results showing how closely the customer data matches
known fraud patterns.
Fraud Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2025. All Rights Reserved.
Page 31
fraudNetworkAuthenticationRe
sult
A FraudNetworkAuthenticationResult. Contains the results
of network authentication verification checks performed
during fraud evaluation. Provides the authentication status
indicating whether the network connection and calling
party have been successfully verified through
telecommunications network authentication mechanisms,
helping to identify potential spoofing or unauthorized
access attempts.
fraudProfileMatchResult
A FraudProfileMatchResult. Contains the results of
customer profile matching analysis performed against
fraud pattern databases and watchlists. Provides an
overall global match score indicating the strength of
correlation with known fraud profiles, along with detailed
matching results for individual profile elements (such as
name, email, address) showing which specific data points
matched and their individual confidence scores. This
helps identify customers or transactions that closely
resemble known fraudulent patterns.
fraudRiskProfileResult
A FraudRiskProfileResult. Contains the actual values and
status information for risk profile factors retrieved from
the telecommunications system during fraud evaluation.
Provides concrete data such as tenure durations (for SIM,
device, and line expressed as Duration with flexible time
units), payment method registered with the telco, call
forwarding settings, current service status, account holder
role, and recent SIM swap activity. This information is used
to assess the fraud risk level based on customer account
characteristics and usage patterns.
fraudScoreResult
A FraudScoreResult. Contains the calculated fraud risk
score and supporting information from the fraud scoring
algorithm. Provides a numerical score indicating the level
of fraud risk detected (typically on a scale like 0-100,
where higher values indicate greater fraud risk) along with
an optional textual explanation describing the key factors
that influenced the score, such as credit history,
transaction patterns, or behavioral anomalies.

Page 33
globalMatchScore
A String. Overall aggregated match score indicating the
strength of correlation between the customer profile and
known fraud patterns, typically expressed as a string to
accommodate various scoring systems (percentage like
'90', decimal like '0.90', categorical like 'HIGH', or qualified
ranges like '85-95'). The calculation methodology may
vary by implementation but commonly uses weighted
averaging, maximum value, or composite algorithms based
on individual profileMatch element scores. For example, if
profileMatch contains email:'95', name:'85', address:'80',
the global score might be '90' (weighted average) or '95'
(highest match) depending on the fraud detection
system’s algorithm.
profileMatch
A ProfileMatch [0..*]. Array of profile matches.

ProfileMatch sub-resource fields
Represents the matching analysis result for a single customer profile element during fraud
detection. Identifies which specific profile attribute (such as name, email, phone number, or
address) was evaluated and provides a numerical score indicating how closely it matches
against
reference
fraud
patterns
or
watchlist
entries.
Higher
scores
indicate
stronger
matches and potentially higher fraud risk for that particular profile element.
matchElement
A String. The specific customer profile attribute being
evaluated for matching against fraud patterns. Common
examples include 'name', 'email', 'address', 'phoneNumber',
or other identifying customer information that can be
compared against fraud databases or watchlists.
Fraud Management User Guide
© TM Forum 2025. All Rights Reserved.
Page 34
matchScore
A String. Match confidence score for this profile element,
expressed as a string to support multiple scoring formats
used by different fraud detection systems. Common
formats include: percentage strings ('90', '85.5'), decimal
confidence scores ('0.90'), categorical ratings ('HIGH',
'MEDIUM', 'LOW'), or qualified scores ('90-EXACT', '75-
FUZZY'). String type provides flexibility for fraud detection
vendors to use their native scoring systems while
maintaining API compatibility. Numerical percentage
interpretation: 0-100 where higher values indicate
stronger matches and greater fraud likelihood, with 100
representing a perfect match.

API NOTIFICATIONS
For
every
single
of
operation
on
the
entities
use
the
following
templates
and
provide
sample REST notification POST calls.
It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in
the REST Guidelines reproduced below.
Register listener
POST /hub
Description
Sets
the
communication
endpoint
address
the
service
instance
must
use
to
deliver
information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST
calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case
DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.
Request
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
 
"callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
Response
201
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42

Unregister listener
DELETE /hub/{id}
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.
Request
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
Response
204

Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.
Provides
to
a
registered
listener
the
description
of
the
event
that
was
raised.
The
/client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.
